target_customer: Independent and regional restaurant brands wanting to expand through delivery kitchens, later restaurant operators buying software
problem: Independent restaurants struggled to expand and profit in delivery. Byte Kitchen licensed their brands into shared digital food halls called Noshery, then pivoted to selling its operating software.
business_model: Brand licensing and food hall operations, later restaurant operations SaaS
product_category: Digital food halls and restaurant operating software

founders.name: Quinn McKenna
founders.background_notes: About 30 years in restaurants, opened 30+, former California Restaurant Association director

competitors.name: Nextbite
competitors.what: Connects virtual restaurant brands to restaurants with spare kitchen capacity
competitors.traction_then: described as the best capitalized virtual restaurant player

competitors.name: Reef Kitchens
competitors.what: Parking lot delivery kitchens powering virtual brands
competitors.traction_then: launched virtual brands including Another Wing in Nov 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: Operations heavy food business at first, with modest software. The software became the product later.

defensibility.rationale: Food hall and ghost kitchen models were widely copied and capital intensive. Restaurant software later gives mild switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not shown to have been copied. YC lists the company as acquired but no buyer or date was found.

market_need_then: The 2020 to 2021 delivery boom pushed restaurants toward virtual brands and shared kitchens, and press covered ghost kitchens heavily in 2021.

branding.brand_signature: Noshery, the name of its virtual food hall locations

brand_strength.rationale: Local trade press covered the Noshery halls, but no source shows consumer pull. The parent name is generic and the product later changed to software.

pivots.from: Licensing restaurant brands into Noshery digital food halls
pivots.why: Not explained in the source; the article only says greener pastures

outcome_analysis: Byte Kitchen licensed restaurant brands into Noshery food halls in San Mateo and San Carlos and raised about 6 million dollars in August 2022 during the end of the ghost kitchen boom. By 2024 it had scaled to three halls and pivoted to restaurant software. YC lists it as acquired, but the buyer, date and price were not found and the reasons for the exit are not public.
notes: Exit date and acquirer not found; exit date left null. Total raised: HNGRY says just over 6 million; one aggregator says 16.18 million, unverified. Sources split on stage label seed versus Series A. Pivot date is the article's 'earlier in 2024' and is approximate. The website still operates as ByteKitchen with named tools ByteCheck, ByteCater, BytePrep and ByteShift. Name origin not found.
